newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's YUKOS plans $300 mln new share offerings.
newsitem.headline: Russia's YUKOS plans $300 mln new share offerings.

text.p: Russia's YUKOS oil company, parent of Yuganskneftegaz, plans to raise $300 million in three stock offerings to partially cover 4.35 trillion roubles ($809 million) in debts, the company said on Monday.
"In principle we plan three offerings to bring in $300 million dollars," YUKOS board member Konstantin Kogalovsky, first vice chairman of Bank Menatep, told a news conference.
Stockholders at an extraordinary meeting on Saturday approved one new issue to increase the number of YUKOS shares by 35 percent and raise $100 million, he said.
Stockholders also gave the board of directors of YUKOS, which is controled by Menatep, power to make the new issues without further approval, a company statement said.
YUKOS Vice President Sergei Generalov said the first issue would be used to pay 350 billion roubles in back wages and part of the four trillion roubles owed to the government.
The second and third issues, if approved, will be used to pay more of the government debt.
Kogalovsky said the first offering was planned for October 30 and would take about two months to complete, after which YUKOS will formally consider two further offerings, he said.
"The (final) decision has not been made," he added.
The company will sell 580 million new shares for 909 roubles per four-rouble nominal share in the first round.
Kogalovsky said the company calculated that 909 roubles was fair market price, based on the price of shares at a closed auction of 7.9 percent of YUKOS stock in May.
Current shareholders would be entitled to buy new shares in order to retain their current proportion of company holdings at a 10 percent discount on market price, he added.

Any shares not bought by current shareholders would be offered through Bank Menatep to further investors. Kogalovsky said foreigners could buy shares but were not allowed a controlling interest in YUKOS.
YUKOS is not listed on the Russian Trading System, but its Yuganskneftegaz subsidiary is traded.
But a broker quoted YUKOS on Monday at 24-26 U.S. cents after a 250-1 share split approved by shareholders on Saturday.
After the split and the new issue YUKOS will have 2.2 billion shares and authorised capital of 8.9 billion roubles.
AOOT NK YUKOS is one of around a dozen vertically integrated oil companies set up in recent years. Yuganskneftegaz unit is Russia's second-largest oil producer.
In a December 1995, Menatep won a 33 percent stake in YUKOS and the right to manage an additional 45 percent owned formally by the government.
Kogalovsky said Menatep, which as of September 1 has the right for three years to sell the government shares, would not do so soon.
In three years, without hurrying, we will decide when it is best to sell them," he said. ($1 = 5,377 roubles)
--Peter Henderson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
